why: Quote verified verbatim at skills.md:539, but that line has four sentences and the finding read only the first. Both halves of the claimed divergence fail. CITATION: base-agent.ts:2391 is a bare closing brace inside latestSkillSelections; the real gates are :2405 (runtime?.provider !== 'pi') and :2411 (!skill?.pluginRuntime), inside materializeRuntimeSkillContext (:2401). HALF 1 (scope): that our host executor runs only for plugin skills is the recorded deliberate posture, not drift. The parity audit's Deliberate-differences table (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1547) states 'No shell execution from skill/command bundle text (!`cmd`, @file detected and deferred) | Keeps a prompt-injection and supply-chain surface closed. The defect is the silence, not the refusal', and the closure is visible in code: format-adapters/claude.ts:655 classifies !`...` as bash-execution and emits a plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution diagnostic (:741-749), so custom commands are detected-and-deferred, not silently dropped. The narrow re-opening for plugin skills is its own recorded unit — commit b83ccd05 'feat(plugins): activate portable plugin peripherals', plan step 5 'Govern skill shell context' (docs/current-plans/pi-claude-post-parity.md at that commit), which specifies exactly the executor contract, the 32 KiB cap and the 5 s timeout now in capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts. HALF 1 is also factually wrong about the Claude backend: claude-agent.ts:305 passes settingSources ['user','project','local'] to the Claude Agent SDK and claude-agent.ts:1627-1628 sets plugins: [] because 'skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute'. Per agent-sdk/skills.md:20 and :28 the SDK itself discovers and loads user/project skills from ~/.claude/skills and .claude/skills under those very setting sources, so on that backend the SDK owns the substitution — 'any skill on the Claude backend never executes its command' is not established and is contradicted by who owns the path. HALF 2 (kill switch): the identifier is genuinely absent from our TypeScript (0 hits in *.ts under packages/apps/scripts), but the consequence is false twice over. (a) On the Claude backend the setting IS live: it is declared in the shipped SDK's own settings type, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:4922 'Disable inline shell execution in skills and custom slash commands from user, project, or plugin sources', and is present in the claude binary and in the bundled apps/electron/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js — with settingSources user/project/local the SDK reads it from the same settings.json the page names. (b) On Pi, where our own executor runs, an administrator CAN forbid skill-originated shell — this is the 'enforcement one layer up' trap. SessionManager.runtimeSkillContextExecutor (:4521) authorizes every command as a Bash call carrying semanticId 'skill-context' (:4670-4674) against capabilityRuntime.managedPermissionDsl (:4580), which is this.managedPiPolicy.permissionDsl (:4096) — the admin-delivered managed policy, applied with managedPermissionRulesOnly. permission-dsl.ts:648 matches {kind:'tool', semanticId} against request.semanticId, so a managed rule {action:'deny', match:{kind:'tool', semanticId:'skill-context'}} denies exactly this capability and nothing else; a bash-kind deny covers it too. On deny the executor throws before any spawn and writes a receipt outcome 'denied' / code 'permission_denied' / isolationProfile 'not-started' (:4683-4686), and SessionManager.process-supervisor.test.ts:341-371 is the positive control for a managed DSL deny blocking the sibling command-hook runner on the identical wiring. So the kill switch the page recommends exists here under this fork's own admin surface (managed permission DSL + per-capability plugin toggles, itself a recorded deliberate difference in the audit's section 4) rather than under Claude's settings key name. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3, but the same file's addendum documents the provider === 'pi' gating pattern this finding rediscovered.
correctedState: The quoted sentence is real (skills.md:539), but the divergence is not. (1) Scope: our host-side executor deliberately runs only for plugin skills on the Pi runtime — the closed-by-default posture is recorded in the parity audit's Deliberate-differences table (:1547, prompt-injection and supply-chain containment) and the narrow governed re-opening is commit b83ccd05, plan step 5 'Govern skill shell context'. Custom commands are detected and visibly deferred, not silently ignored (format-adapters/claude.ts:655, :741-749). On the Claude backend the Claude Agent SDK owns skill loading and substitution (settingSources ['user','project','local'] at claude-agent.ts:305, plugins: [] at :1628; agent-sdk/skills.md:20,:28), so the claim that no skill executes there is unfounded. (2) Kill switch: `disableSkillShellExecution` has no reader in our TypeScript, but it is declared and honored by the bundled Claude Agent SDK (sdk.d.ts:4922) on the Claude backend, and on Pi the same capability is admin-deniable through this fork's managed permission DSL — every skill-context command is authorized as Bash with semanticId 'skill-context' against managedPiPolicy.permissionDsl (SessionManager.ts:4580, :4670-4674; matcher at permission-dsl.ts:648), throwing before spawn with a 'permission_denied' receipt. Correct citation for the gates is base-agent.ts:2405 and :2411, not :2391.
